mechanistic interpretability, made tangible

What if a model had dials?

A small intervention at a specific point in a language model can tilt what it notices, writes, or says. Explore the idea by pushing a toy model's neurons around.

Read this firstThis is a teaching simulation, not a live Qwen model. It borrows the vocabulary and workflow of the referenced research so you can build intuition without running a model or changing real weights.

the mental model

A neuron is less like a thought, more like a tiny vote.

01 / SCAN

Find a signal

Run many prompts through the model and look for units whose activity or output clusters around a theme.

02 / STEER

Push or pull

Add a small vector at the unit's output. The weights stay put; the activation is nudged for this run.

03 / COMPARE

Keep the rollout

Compare the same prompt across doses. The interesting bit is the difference—not a single dramatic sample.
